superseded.action: no pin added -- the vllm==0.17.1-bundled Qwen3_5MoeConfig/Qwen3_5MoeTextConfig shim (vllm/transformers_utils/configs/qwen3_5_moe.py) was judged sufficient because it resolves the ARCHITECTURE independently of transformers. That was correct for the architecture and wrong for the TOKENIZER: real canary pod gx5b5cakrhp359 (2026-09-04, 2xH100) shows vLLM resolving the architecture fine and then dying on `ValueError: Tokenizer class TokenizersBackend does not exist or is not currently imported` (transformers/models/auto/tokenization_auto.py via vllm/tokenizers/hf.py). The bundled vllm config shim never touches tokenizer loading -- that always goes through the image's real transformers, and vllm 0.17.1's image ships a 4.x transformers (bounded '>= 4.56.0, < 5' by requirements/common.txt) that has no TokenizersBackend class at all (that class lives in transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py, added in the v5.x line). This block is kept, not deleted, so the wrong conclusion and the evidence that overturned it both stay on the record.

framework_floor_audit.required: The checkpoint's tokenizer_config.json declares tokenizer_class=TokenizersBackend, a class that only exists in transformers v5.x (src/transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py; imported by tokenization_auto.py as `if is_tokenizers_available(): from ...tokenization_utils_tokenizers import TokenizersBackend else: TokenizersBackend = None`). transformers v5.3.0 -- the checkpoint's own declared transformers_version -- already carries CONFIG_MAPPING_NAMES['qwen3_5_moe'] = 'Qwen3_5MoeConfig' and TOKENIZER_MAPPING_NAMES entries for both 'qwen3_5' and 'qwen3_5_moe' pointing at Qwen3_5Tokenizer (conditioned on is_tokenizers_available()), confirmed unchanged at v5.4.0 too. So the framework that has to resolve BOTH the architecture and the tokenizer is a real transformers >= 5.x, not vllm's bundled config-only shim -- the 2026-09-03 audit only checked the architecture half.
framework_floor_audit.image_ships: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.17.1 bounds transformers '>= 4.56.0, < 5' (requirements/common.txt) -- structurally incapable of ever importing TokenizersBackend, independent of exactly which 4.x release is installed. Its model_executor/models/registry.py does register Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration (unchanged fact, still true), and that is why vLLM got past architecture resolution and only died on the tokenizer.
framework_floor_audit.action: Bumped base_image to vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.0-ubuntu2404@sha256:69234fc31ff1d5e1687b2f06bba39e0f8c58dd4755f0508dbe0595cd3692b851 -- the exact digest glm_ocr already proved live on RunPod on 2026-09-03/04 -- and added the same --no-deps pin glm_ocr uses on top of it: transformers==5.4.0, tokenizers==0.22.2, huggingface_hub==1.5.0, hf-xet==1.3.2. Verified transformers==5.4.0 still maps qwen3_5_moe in CONFIG_MAPPING_NAMES/TOKENIZER_MAPPING_NAMES and still exports TokenizersBackend, and vllm==0.19.0 still registers Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration and still ships vllm/transformers_utils/configs/qwen3_5_moe.py with Qwen3_5MoeConfig/Qwen3_5MoeTextConfig (model_type qwen3_5_moe_text unchanged), so the 2026-09-03 preflight's vLLM-registry and bundled-config checks stay valid and were kept; a transformers-side check (CONFIG_MAPPING_NAMES membership + TokenizersBackend importability) was added ahead of them, and the whole preflight now runs before the 70.21 GB weight download (fetching only config.json + tokenizer_config.json via hf_hub_download) instead of after.

cuda_floor.vendor_documented_floor: none published: the vendor documents no driver floor beyond the image's own CUDA runtime
cuda_floor.rationale: min_cuda_version is the lowest CUDA version a RunPod host may report for this runtime to start. It is sent as the create payload's allowedCudaVersions -- every version RunPod lists at or above it -- because pod 3xag0y00rgoj4n (glm_ocr) ran a CUDA 12.9 image on a host reporting cudaVersion 12.8 and died in torch._C._cuda_init with CUDA error 804 after the pod was already billing. Read anonymously from the pinned image's own OCI config blob at the digest runtime.json pins; nothing is inferred from the image name.
